documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seven weeks out from the pituitary surgery. Energy slowly coming back. Face less full, he says pants are looser. Back soreness easing. Nose healed. On hydrocortisone 10 BID, no missed doses, no illnesses. Neurosurgery post-op visit went fine. Endocrinology next week.

Pack a day.

Exam: BP 140/88, better than the fall. Weight down a bit more. Face less round. Striae fading to pink. Lungs clear. Heart regular.

A/P
- Cushing disease s/p resection, on replacement hydrocortisone - endocrinology to taper.
- HTN improving, continue lisinopril 10.
- T2DM: A1c 7.0 today, coming down from 7.4. Metformin same.
- Lung screening CT due in March - ordered.
- Tobacco counseled.

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology Clinic - 02/04/2025
Re: Eric Strong

Dear Doctor,

Mr. Strong is eight weeks past transsphenoidal resection of his ACTH-staining adenoma. The post-operative morning cortisol of 1.2 ug/dL indicates remission. He feels better week by week; weight is down to 103 kg. No symptoms of under-replacement.

Current: hydrocortisone 10 mg twice daily, metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10, atorvastatin 20, olanzapine 10 qhs, vitamin D3 1000 units. NKDA.

Plan:
- Reduce hydrocortisone to 10 mg each morning only. Sick-day rules unchanged.
- I'll check a morning cortisol off hydrocortisone in a few months to see if his own adrenal function has recovered.
- Bone: DXA showed low bone mass (L2-L4 T -2.2, femoral neck -1.7, total hip -1.3). Bone density usually recovers substantially once cortisol is normal, so I'll hold off on bone medication and repeat DXA a year after remission, around November 2026. Continue vitamin D and dietary calcium.
- Diabetes: metformin unchanged.

Sincerely,
Endocrinology

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening

Indication: annual lung cancer screening, current smoker.
Technique: low-dose noncontrast chest CT.
Comparison: 03/12/2024.
Findings: No pulmonary nodules. Lungs clear. Central airways patent. No effusion. Normal heart size, no pericardial effusion. No adenopathy. Known L1 compression deformity.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1: negative. Annual low-dose CT in 12 months.

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology Clinic - 06/10/2025
Re: Eric Strong

Dear Doctor,

Mr. Strong held his hydrocortisone for 24 hours before this morning's draw. Morning cortisol 11.6 ug/dL - his own adrenal function has recovered.

He feels well. Weight 99 kg. Cushingoid features have largely resolved. Back pain gone.

Plan:
- Stop hydrocortisone. Keep a few tablets at home for the next couple of months in case of serious illness, and call us if he becomes very fatigued, lightheaded or nauseated.
- Cushing disease in remission. Yearly surveillance for recurrence; next visit in about a year with a 24-hour urine free cortisol.
- Repeat DXA in November 2026. Continue vitamin D.
- Metformin unchanged.

Allergies: NKDA.

Sincerely,
Endocrinology

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Emergency Department, community hospital
Seen 10/17/2025
Patient: Eric Strong, 51M

CC: black stools, upper abdominal pain.

HPI: Black, tarry stools for two days with a dull, gnawing ache in the upper abdomen that wakes him at night. Eating eases it for a while, then it comes back worse. No vomiting, no blood in vomit, no lightheadedness at rest. History of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, metabolic syndrome, schizophrenia and an ACTH-producing pituitary adenoma. Takes lisinopril and atorvastatin, olanzapine 10 mg nightly, and uses over-the-counter ibuprofen now and then for chronic knee pain.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: current smoker, about a pack a day since 15. Weekend alcohol, 1-2 drinks. Office manager.
Family: father died of lung cancer at 60; mother with hypertension and hyperlipidemia.

Exam: BP 130/85, HR 98. Pale. Abdomen soft with mild epigastric tenderness, no rebound, no guarding. Rectal: black stool, guaiac positive.

Labs: hemoglobin 10.2 g/dL, hematocrit 30.5%, MCV 86 fL. BUN 29, creatinine 1.0. Liver enzymes normal. INR normal.

ED course: two large-bore IVs, IV pantoprazole bolus and infusion. Ibuprofen held. GI consulted. Heart rate down to 90 on reassessment. No transfusion needed.

Impression: upper GI bleed, likely peptic ulcer in setting of NSAID use.
Disposition: admitted to medicine for endoscopy.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

reports.text:
Specimen: gastric antrum and body biopsies.
Microscopic: gastric mucosa without significant inflammation. No Helicobacter pylori organisms identified on routine and immunohistochemical staining. No intestinal metaplasia, dysplasia or malignancy.
reports.conclusion: Gastric mucosa, negative for Helicobacter pylori. No dysplasia or malignancy.

documents.title: Upper endoscopy report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
EGD 10/18/2025, inpatient
Indication: melena, Hgb 10.2
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care.
Findings: Esophagus normal. Stomach normal, no blood in the stomach; antrum and body biopsied for H. pylori. Duodenal bulb: 1 cm ulcer with a clean base, no visible vessel, no adherent clot, no active bleeding. Second portion normal.
Therapy: none required.
Impression: duodenal bulb ulcer, clean base. Likely NSAID related.
Plan: PPI twice daily for 8 weeks, no NSAIDs, follow biopsy results.

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Community hospital - Medicine
Admitted 10/17/2025, discharged 10/19/2025
Patient: Eric Strong, 51M

Principal diagnosis: bleeding duodenal ulcer, NSAID-related.
Secondary: blood-loss anemia; hypertension; type 2 diabetes; hyperlipidemia; schizophrenia, stable; history of Cushing disease, pituitary adenoma resected 12/2024.

Course: Presented with two days of melena and epigastric pain, Hgb 10.2, BUN 29. Treated with IV pantoprazole. EGD 10/18 showed a 1 cm clean-based duodenal bulb ulcer, no active bleeding, no endoscopic treatment. Gastric biopsies sent for H. pylori - negative (final 10/21). Hemoglobin 9.7 on 10/18 and 9.9 on the day of discharge; no transfusion. Tolerating diet, stools turning brown, pain much improved.

Discharge medications:
- Pantoprazole 40 mg twice daily x 8 weeks (NEW)
- Acetaminophen 500 mg, 1-2 tabs up to three times daily as needed for knee pain (NEW)
- STOP ibuprofen and all NSAIDs (Advil, Motrin, Aleve, aspirin products)
- Continue metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 10, atorvastatin 20, olanzapine 10 qhs, vitamin D3
Allergies: NKDA

Follow-up: PCP within a week with CBC. Return for black stools, vomiting blood, fainting.
